paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
model_annotation: The plot shows training loss as a function of iteration for six model configurations (Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128)), illustrating how each curve decreases over the course of training. The x-axis is labeled “#Iteration” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140,000, with regularly spaced tick labels at 20,000-iteration intervals. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” and uses a linear scale spanning approximately 2.4 to 3.4 with tick labels spaced by 0.1. Each series is drawn as a solid line with no point markers, and each line is accompanied by a faint, same-colored shaded band around it. The purple Vanilla curve starts above 3.4 near iteration 0, drops steeply in the early iterations, and gradually declines to about 2.45 by 140,000. The light-blue StrmLLM (n=64) curve also begins above 3.4, decreases rapidly at first, then more slowly, ending around 2.60 at 140,000. The orange SepLLM (n=64) curve begins above 3.4, falls quickly early on, and continues decreasing to roughly 2.52 by the end. The green SepLLM (n=64, H) curve follows a similar shape, starting above 3.4 and ending near about 2.51–2.52 at 140,000. The red SepLLM (n=64, H/T) curve starts above 3.4, declines steeply early, and finishes at approximately 2.49 by 140,000. The dark-blue SepLLM (n=128) curve begins above 3.4, decreases rapidly initially, then tapers to around 2.55 at 140,000, with all curves showing their largest drop near the beginning of the iteration range and slower changes later.
